claim: John D'Oyly's Sinhala language training, knowledge of Kandyan customs and cultivated intelligence contacts gave British policy an operational means to deepen elite discord and politically isolate Sri Vikrama Rajasinghe before the 1815 settlement.
bounded_by: Knowledge and intelligence were contributing mechanisms, not a sufficient single cause; military pressure, royal violence and unpopularity, factional ambitions and British coercive capacity also mattered.
notes: Closes the bridge between defence-in-depth and political conquest without reverting to an elite-betrayal monocause.
